title: Management and Supervision
before:
1. Accountability for the site rests with a single role. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

2. Within that accountability, operational control is delegated by shift. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.

3. On each shift the chain of command remains explicit. Floor staff report to the shift supervisor on duty for tasking, priorities and immediate decisions.

Across shifts the warehouse manager retains ultimate authority for operations, safety and final sign-offs. No parallel approval route overrides that accountability.

4. Certain decisions are reserved to the warehouse manager and cannot be delegated. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.

Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, stock controllers prepare counts and recounts, but closure requires warehouse-manager sign-off before results become final.

5. Financial authority for loss follows a clear threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

In practice the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Lower-value cases follow the approval route defined in Chapter 2.

6. Working-time authority is similarly reserved. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.

Before any overtime is worked, supervisors submit the request for warehouse-manager approval. Overtime worked without that approval is not authorised.

7. Authorisation to operate handling equipment is a safety-critical sign-off. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

Following training and assessment under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, the warehouse manager grants the individual authorisation. Without it, operation of forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks is prohibited.

8. Incident ownership sits with shift leadership. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report.

Immediately after containment and first response on the shift, the shift supervisor examines the report for completeness, assigns corrective actions and escalates safety matters to the warehouse manager.

9. Coordination between the two levels works as follows:

(a) At shift start, the shift supervisor assumes responsibility for floor staff and incident response;
(b) During the shift, the shift supervisor decides routine operational and safety responses;
(c) Where a matter requires a reserved sign-off, the shift supervisor escalates to the warehouse manager for operations, safety and final sign-offs.

Reserved matters include stocktake sign-off, damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR, overtime approval and authorisation of new forklift operators.

10. Records of all reserved decisions are retained for audit. Sign-offs for stocktake results, write-offs above 500 EUR, overtime and new forklift operator authorisations identify the warehouse manager as approver, while incident reviews identify the reviewing shift supervisor.

title: Approvals and Sign-offs
before:
1. Damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR: approval by the shift supervisor is required before disposal, resale or system adjustment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

Within this band the shift supervisor checks the damage report, photographs and quantity, confirms the value calculation, and records the approval in the system. No goods leave the quarantine area in Zone F without that recorded approval.

2. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR: approval by the warehouse manager is required before disposal, resale or system adjustment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

Above the 500 EUR threshold the warehouse manager reviews the same evidence, confirms insurance notification where applicable, and authorises the final write-off value. Floor staff must escalate the case file unchanged when the threshold is exceeded.

3. Stocktake results: sign-off by the warehouse manager only is permitted under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

Following the final recount and reconciliation, stock controllers submit counts, variances and proposed adjustments for review. Without warehouse-manager sign-off, no adjustment is posted to inventory.

4. Inspected returns: final disposition approved by the shift supervisor under PR-07 Returns handling.

After returns staff in Zone F have inspected the goods and proposed restock, rework or scrap, the shift supervisor validates condition, system status and reason code. Restock to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E proceeds only after this disposition is recorded.

5. Overtime: approval by the warehouse manager only is permitted for any additional hours beyond Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

Requests state reason, zone, headcount and duration, and are submitted before the overtime is worked. Unapproved hours are not rostered and are returned for rescheduling within normal shifts.

6. Dock doors and time slots: assignment by the dispatcher governs all arrivals and departures under PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

Carriers receive a confirmed door among dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving or dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch, with a fixed arrival window. Inbound operators and dispatchers work only to the current assignment board.

7. Incident reports: review by the shift supervisor is mandatory for every report.

Immediately after containment and first aid where needed, the shift supervisor examines statements, equipment logs and zone conditions, determines corrective action, and forwards cases requiring site-level decisions to the warehouse manager. Accountability for the whole site, including operations, safety and final sign-offs, remains with the warehouse manager.

8. New forklift operators: authorisation by the warehouse manager only permits operation of forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Authorisation follows valid licence evidence, internal assessment and documented induction. Until the warehouse-manager authorisation is entered on the authorised-operator list, the candidate must not operate any truck unsupervised.

title: Quarantine and Write-offs
before:
1. Apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling to every pallet, carton and item found damaged, leaking, crushed or otherwise unfit for normal stock.

2. Move the affected goods to quarantine without delay. Segregate the damaged quantity from saleable stock at the point of discovery and transfer it under control to the quarantine area.

3. Retain all goods awaiting a damaged-goods decision in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not return quarantined goods to bulk, pick faces or dispatch until PR-09 Damaged-goods handling releases them.

4. Note that Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep quarantine segregated from inspection, rework and labelling work within that area so quarantined goods cannot be mixed with goods under rework.

5. Record the damage at quarantine receipt. Enter the product identity, quantity, location of discovery, nature of damage and photographic evidence where the procedure requires it, and link the record to the original inbound, storage, picking or returns task.

6. Protect the quarantined goods while they are held. Stack them stably, keep access routes clear, prevent further damage and isolate any goods that present a leakage or contamination risk until assessed.

7. Propose restock, rework or scrap for each quarantined line in accordance with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Submit the proposal with the supporting evidence and quantity for approval before any disposal, rework instruction or system adjustment.

8. Obtain approval for every write-off before posting it. Present the value of the damaged goods and the proposed scrap quantity to the authorised approver and record the decision.

9. Escalate write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager. Do not scrap, dispose of or adjust goods above that value without that approval.

10. Request approval from the shift supervisor for write-offs up to 500 EUR. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and decides these lower-value cases during the shift.

11. Refer write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for final decision. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and provides the final sign-off on higher-value losses.

12. Execute only the approved disposition. Complete rework through the defined route, return approved restock to stock through the system, or scrap approved goods securely and post the write-off after the required approval is recorded.

13. Close the quarantine record after physical completion. Confirm that the approved quantity has been reworked, restocked or scrapped, that the system reflects the outcome, and that no residual quantity remains in the quarantine area in Zone F.

14. Review quarantine holdings each shift. Chase overdue proposals, overdue approvals and overdue disposals, and keep the quarantine area clear for new arrivals requiring assessment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

title: Spills and Damaged Goods
before:
1. Stop work around any spill or fallen load and secure the immediate area against forklift and pedestrian movement.
2. Put on high-visibility vests before entering the affected area, as high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
3. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor during the entire spill response and damaged-goods handling operation.
4. Execute PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every chemical, oil, chilled-liquid or unknown-substance spill without deviation.
5. Contain liquids with the nearest spill kit, prevent entry into drains and aisles, and ventilate the area where the procedure requires it.
6. Never touch, repack or move leaking hazmat containers with bare hands and never place suspect containers into normal storage.
7. Alert the shift supervisor immediately after containment, since the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
8. Execute PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for crushed cartons, broken pallets, torn wrapping, wet stock and any goods contaminated by a spill.
9. Photograph the damage, record product, quantity, location, time and suspected cause, and keep the pallet intact for inspection.
10. Transfer all goods awaiting a damaged-goods decision to the quarantine area in Zone F and do not restock, rework or scrap them there.
11. Mark the quarantined pallet clearly with damage details and prevent any further movement until a written decision exists.
12. Obtain approval for the write-off before posting it in the system, in line with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
13. Submit write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor, who approves damaged-goods write-offs up to that value.
14. Escalate write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager, since damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.
15. Understand that the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR and no other role may substitute that sign-off.
16. Hand over open spill clean-ups and quarantined pallets at shift change with quantities, locations and actions taken fully documented.
17. Reinspect the cleaned floor, racking and adjacent stock for hidden damage before releasing the area back to normal operation.
18. Replace used spill materials, report depleted kits for replenishment, and confirm that quarantined stock remains segregated in Zone F.

title: Incident Reporting
before:
1. Report every injury, collision, rack damage, dock damage, fire alarm activation and near miss at once to the supervisor on duty. Do not wait until the end of the task and do not leave the scene unsafe.

2. Notify the shift supervisor directly by radio or in person. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Follow the instructions given and preserve the area for inspection where safe to do so.

3. Record the incident in the incident report before leaving the floor. State time, place, persons involved, equipment involved, witnesses and a factual description of what happened. Attach photographs where the reporting form provides for them.

4. Submit every incident report for review without delay. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Correct incomplete reports immediately when they are returned and resubmit them within the same duty period.

5. Escalate serious injury, major damage, operational shutdown and any release covered by PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to the warehouse manager through the shift supervisor. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

6. Treat damaged stock only under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Segregate affected pallets and cartons, label them clearly and prevent further movement until a disposition decision is recorded.

7. Obtain write-off approval before posting any damaged-goods write-off. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. Send larger cases to the warehouse manager with the inspection record and photographs attached.

8. Observe the 500 EUR threshold strictly. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR. Do not split one damage event into smaller amounts to avoid the higher approval.

9. Include open incidents, damaged-goods cases and spill follow-up actions in PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Brief the incoming shift supervisor face to face on injuries, blocked locations, quarantined stock and equipment taken out of service.

10. Check that the handover log records report numbers, approver names and pending actions. Carry forward any incident without supervisor review or without required write-off approval as an outstanding item for the next shift.

11. Cooperate fully with investigation and remedial actions. Provide statements on request, attend re-briefing when ordered and apply revised controls from the first task after they are issued.

title: Shift Supervisors
before:
1. Run one shift: floor staff and incident response across all zones during the assigned hours. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

3. Direct work in Zone A, the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection; Zone B, the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking; Zone C, the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks; Zone D, the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8; Zone E, the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C; and Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. performs PR-09 Damaged-goods handling as the binding process for every damage event covered by this agreement.
2. Every pallet, carton or unit showing crushing, puncture, leakage, contamination, tampering or other visible deterioration is treated as damaged goods from discovery.
3. Inside Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, a dedicated quarantine area provides segregated holding for all such goods.
4. Segregated quarantine status blocks any restock, rework, picking or dispatch until inspection and a documented disposition decision are complete.
5. Promptly after transfer to quarantine, inspection findings, quantities, locations and supporting evidence are recorded in the warehouse system against the client account.
6. Notification describing the affected products, quantities held and preliminary cause is issued to the client without undue delay.
7. Disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling is limited to return to stock, rework, return to supplier or scrap on documented client instruction.
8. Restock, rework or scrap movements are executed only after the disposition has been approved and recorded.
9. Financial write-off authority for damaged goods follows a fixed two-tier threshold agreed for this service.
10. Up to 500 EUR per damage event, the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs.
11. Above 500 EUR per damage event, the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs.
12. Accordingly, the applicable approval is obtained before any corresponding write-off is posted in the system.
13. Separately, splitting of a single damage event into smaller amounts to use a lower approval tier is not permitted.
14. Clients receive a complete case file for each event, linking the damage report, quarantine location, disposition approval and financial posting.
15. Traceability is preserved from initial discovery through final clearance of the quarantine record.
16. Unresolved quarantine holdings are reviewed regularly and escalated for client direction before any further action.
17. Direct costs of inspection, storage in quarantine, rework or disposal are charged only as agreed in the commercial schedule.
18. Liability for damaged goods remains as set out in the liability provisions of this agreement and is unaffected by the operational handling described here.
19. Jointly, the parties will use damage trends from quarantine records to reduce recurrence and improve packaging and handling controls.
